# Spark Powered

> How to keep a US home running in a power outage with a portable power station or home battery: how to connect one to the house, what it runs and for how long, and which unit fits which job. Written by Geoff Baron (https://sparkpowered.com/about), who is not an electrician: every page is researched from the makers' manuals and spec sheets and from official sources (NEC, CPSC, OSHA, DOE, EIA), ends with a dated source list, and has not been hands-on tested. Contact: geoff@mylastlap.com.

Site: https://sparkpowered.com
Language: English (US)
Audience: US homeowners and renters planning for power outages.

## Connecting a battery to the house

- [How to connect a power station to your house safely](https://sparkpowered.com/home-backup): Extension cords, inlet box plus interlock kit, manual transfer switch, or the maker's smart panel: what each powers, which need a licensed electrician and permit, what NEC Article 702 asks for (702.4 user-selected load, 702.5 transfer equipment, the inlet sign for bonded vs floating neutral), the bonded-neutral GFCI problem (Generac), which station outlet feeds which inlet (L14-30R, 14-50R, TT-30R), a worked runtime example, and the backfeeding warning (CPSC, OSHA). No prices. Not hands-on tested; sources read 2026-11-24.
- [Home backup hookup picker](https://sparkpowered.com/home-backup/hookup-picker): Five questions (what must stay on, 120 V only or 240 V loads like a well pump, own or rent, budget, hiring a licensed electrician) to the way to connect a portable power station to a house (extension cords, inlet box + interlock kit, manual transfer switch, or the maker's panel kit such as the Bluetti Apex 300 Home Integration Kit), the battery size (EIA and EWEB loads, 85% usable), in-stock Anker SOLIX, Bluetti, Growatt and ALLPOWERS models that fit (120/240 V or two units on the maker's hub for 240 V loads), and a parts list with cost ranges (HomeGuide 2026, checked 2026-11-14). Renters get cords only; anything at the panel means a licensed electrician and a permit; never backfeed through a wall or dryer outlet.
- [Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus home hookup](https://sparkpowered.com/home-backup/anker-solix-f3800-plus-hookup): From Anker's A1790P manual (PDF pages 6-15): L14-30R 120/240 V 25 A 6,000 W, TT-30R 3,000 W, LRA limit 80 A, 3,840 Wh, the 240 V outlet is off while charging from 120 V. Anker's 30 A 10-circuit switch for one unit (the 50 A one is labeled not for a single Plus), inlet and interlock, or the Home Power Panel; owner reports on bonded vs floating neutral; worked runtime with a 1/2 HP well pump. Read 2026-11-24.
- [Bluetti Apex 300 home hookup](https://sparkpowered.com/home-backup/bluetti-apex-300-hookup): From Bluetti's manual (pages 16-28): 14-50R gives 16 A at 240 V on battery and 50 A only in bypass, 2,764.8 Wh, no motor surge figure (7,680 W Power Lifting is heating-only), motors may start at 2-4x rated power; AT1, Home Integration Kit, interlock or manual switch; neutral question; runtime by Bluetti's own formula. Read 2026-11-24.
- [Home battery backup](https://sparkpowered.com/home-battery-backup): Whole-home installed batteries (Tesla Powerwall 3, Enphase IQ Battery 5P/10C, FranklinWH aPower 2) with EnergySage's market-average installed cost per kWh, versus plug-in whole-home systems and portable stations.

## What it runs, and for how long

- [Power outage backup calculator](https://sparkpowered.com/power-outage-backup-calculator): Essentials (fridge, CPAP, well pump, furnace blower, router, lights) to kWh a day and battery size for 1 to 7 days, with winter solar recharge by state.
- [Power station for a well pump](https://sparkpowered.com/home-backup/well-pump): Calculator from the pump nameplate. Running and starting watts from Franklin Electric's 2026 AIM manual (motor table printed pages 39-41, generator minimum rating page 7, transfer switch rule page 6); which in-stock stations cover the start; F3800 Plus 80 A LRA limit; soft starters (SoftStartUSA, Micro-Air limits, Franklin drive rule); owner reports; transfer switch by a licensed electrician. Read 2026-11-24.
- [Power station for a pellet stove](https://sparkpowered.com/home-backup/pellet-stove): Igniter vs running watts from US Stove (5660, US5522-W), Harman P-Series and PelPro PP130 manuals; hours of heat per in-stock power station; UPS switchover time per model; Harman's back-up sheet on pure sine wave; power-failure smoke warnings from the manuals.
- [Power station for a fridge and freezer](https://sparkpowered.com/power-station-for-refrigerator): Main fridge about 618 kWh a year and separate freezer about 569 (EIA RECS 2020 CE5.3b); starting vs running watts (EWEB, two owner measurements); CDC 4-hour fridge and 48-hour full-freezer rules and a worked outage plan; Frigidaire manual cautions; hours per station with each maker's motor surge figure. No prices.
- [Home battery sizer](https://sparkpowered.com/battery-calculator): kWh of storage needed for a backup goal, the sizing formula, and average daily household use by state, plus 2-4 real systems (portable or installed) that reach that size, with links to each maker for today's price.
- [Generator runtime calculator](https://sparkpowered.com/generator-runtime-calculator): Fuel to store from the generator's rated runtime; carbon monoxide safety (20 feet from the house, CO alarms; CDC, CPSC).
- [Bluetti Elite 200 V2 solar panels](https://sparkpowered.com/home-backup/bluetti-elite-200-v2-solar-panels): Solar input limits from Bluetti's manual (12-60 V Voc, 20 A, 1,000 W, XT60; 8.2 A at 30 V or less in the app's default setting), which Bluetti panels fit in series or parallel, open-circuit voltage math with the NEC 690.7 cold-weather correction (IAEI method), and what a third-party panel needs.
- [What the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 runs](https://sparkpowered.com/power-stations/anker-solix-c1000-gen-2/what-it-runs): Run times on one charge for 15 appliances from 1.02 kWh at 85% usable (2,000 W continuous): typical fridge about 9 hours, CPAP with humidifier 3.5 nights, 1,500 W space heater about 35 minutes, 1/3 HP sump pump about 1 hour of pumping. Cannot run: 12,000 BTU window AC (3,250 W). Watts from EIA RECS 2020, ResMed and the EWEB generator sizing sheet; specs checked November 6, 2026.
- [What the Bluetti AC180 runs](https://sparkpowered.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/what-it-runs): Run times on one charge for 15 appliances from 1.15 kWh at 85% usable (1,800 W continuous): typical fridge about 10 hours, CPAP with humidifier 4 nights, 1,500 W space heater about 40 minutes, 1/3 HP sump pump about 1 hour of pumping. Cannot run: 12,000 BTU window AC (3,250 W); start not confirmed by specs: kitchen refrigerator, chest or upright freezer, 1/3 HP sump pump, 1/3 HP well pump, 1/3 HP furnace blower fan. Watts from EIA RECS 2020, ResMed and the EWEB generator sizing sheet; specs checked October 26, 2026.
- [What the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 runs](https://sparkpowered.com/power-stations/bluetti-elite-200-v2/what-it-runs): Run times on one charge for 15 appliances from 2.07 kWh at 85% usable (2,600 W continuous): typical fridge about 18 hours, CPAP with humidifier 7.5 nights, 1,500 W space heater about 1 hour, 1/3 HP sump pump about 2 hours of pumping. Cannot run: 12,000 BTU window AC (3,250 W); start not confirmed by specs: kitchen refrigerator, chest or upright freezer, 1/3 HP well pump. Watts from EIA RECS 2020, ResMed and the EWEB generator sizing sheet; specs checked November 6, 2026.
- [What the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 runs](https://sparkpowered.com/power-stations/anker-solix-c2000-gen-2/what-it-runs): Run times on one charge for 15 appliances from 2.05 kWh at 85% usable (2,400 W continuous): typical fridge about 18 hours, CPAP with humidifier 7.5 nights, 1,500 W space heater about 1 hour, 1/3 HP sump pump about 2 hours of pumping. Cannot run: 12,000 BTU window AC (3,250 W). Watts from EIA RECS 2020, ResMed and the EWEB generator sizing sheet; specs checked November 6, 2026.
- [What the Bluetti Elite 300 runs](https://sparkpowered.com/power-stations/bluetti-elite-300/what-it-runs): Run times on one charge for 15 appliances from 3.01 kWh at 85% usable (2,400 W continuous): typical fridge about 27 hours, CPAP with humidifier 11 nights, 1,500 W space heater about 1.5 hours, 1/3 HP sump pump about 3 hours of pumping. Cannot run: 12,000 BTU window AC (3,250 W). Watts from EIA RECS 2020, ResMed and the EWEB generator sizing sheet; specs checked November 9, 2026.

## Comparisons (makers' published specs; no prices; some affiliate links)

- [Comparisons](https://sparkpowered.com/compare): Three home-backup comparisons: Growatt HELIOS 3600 vs Bluetti Apex 300, Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus vs Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus, and EcoFlow vs Anker SOLIX size for size.
- [Growatt HELIOS 3600 vs Bluetti Apex 300](https://sparkpowered.com/compare/growatt-helios-3600-vs-bluetti-apex-300): Built on the 240 V question: the Apex 300 gives 120/240 V from one unit (16 A at 240 V on battery, 50 A only in bypass, per Bluetti's manual); the HELIOS 3600 is 120 V and needs two units on Growatt's Double Voltage Power Hub for 240 V (Growatt's wording). Capacity, output, expansion, and outlets from both makers' US stores, read 2026-11-14.
- [Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus vs Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus](https://sparkpowered.com/compare/anker-solix-f3800-plus-vs-jackery-explorer-5000-plus): Two 120/240 V home backup units compared on the makers' published specs.
- [EcoFlow vs Anker SOLIX](https://sparkpowered.com/compare/anker-solix-vs-ecoflow): Power stations compared size for size, up to the DELTA Pro 3 and F3800 Plus, on the makers' published specs.

## Home EV charger questions that come up with home wiring

- [EV charger tripping a GFCI breaker](https://sparkpowered.com/ev-charger-tripping-gfci): Why a plug-in Level 2 EV charger trips a GFCI breaker (NEC 625.54 requires GFCI protection on EV charging receptacles; the charger has its own CCID ground-fault device, about 20 mA per Autel, while a household GFCI trips at about 6 mA per CPSC), what an owner can safely check without opening anything, and why a licensed electrician hardwiring the charger is the usual code-compliant fix (ChargePoint's recommendation). No bypass advice.
- [Extension cord for a Level 2 EV charger](https://sparkpowered.com/ev-charger-extension-cord): Can you use an extension cord with a Level 2 EV charger? No: Tesla (Wall Connector and Mobile Connector manuals), Lectron, Autel and EVIQO all say not to. Why (continuous load, heat at plug joints, warranty), what the 240 V "EV extension cables" sold online are, and the safe options: park closer, a longer-cable charger, or an electrician adding an outlet or hardwiring a charger where you park.

## Notes for citation

- Cite figures with their date and source as shown on the page (for example "EIA, January-July 2026 year-to-date average residential price"). Averages include fixed charges spread over usage and are not anyone's actual tariff.
- US federal incentives changed in 2025. Per the IRS: the new (30D), used (25E) and commercial (45W) clean vehicle credits are not allowed for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025; the charger credit (30C) is not allowed for property placed in service after 30 June 2026; the Residential Clean Energy Credit (25D) is not allowed for expenditures made after 31 December 2025.
- Product specs on the guides and in the Home Battery Sizer are copied from manufacturers' US sites and dated; cite them with that date. We do not list product prices; each product links to the seller's page for today's price.
- Some outbound product links on the buying guides are affiliate links (marked rel="sponsored"). Picks include makers that pay no commission and do not depend on commission. Calculators and state data do not depend on any partner.
